chunk_findings.detail: In `release_mode="auto"`, `asked` is true and `refusal` is called with `also=LR.machine_gates(cfg)`, so missing machine gates are accepted for a release attempt. If an item has its judgement gates recorded but no author identity, `_release_plan` returns `(None, "no author identity...")`; since `release` is false, `_enqueue` falls through to `MQ.add(..., release=None)` and plain-enqueues the item. The normal readiness `refusal` without the machine-gate exemption is never re-run, so an item missing machine gates enters the merge queue as ready when it is not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_add.py:queue_add

chunk_findings.detail: The `_enqueue` docstring says a release that falls short because of a full slot count queues the item without handing it over, but the `except MQ.SlotsFull` branch for `release=True` returns `O.refused(..., queued=False, released=False)` and never retries without a release plan. With `ddflow queue add --release` when the release slot cap is reached, the item is not queued, contradicting the stated behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_add.py:_enqueue

chunk_findings.detail: For a released entry whose `LR.machine_gates(cfg)` includes `"ci"` (the default machine gate), the new loop runs `run_gate(repo, it.id, "ci", agent=agent)` when `"ci" in pipe` and the item does not yet have outcome `"passed"` — the normal release case. Immediately below, the pre-existing `if "ci" in pipe:` block calls `ci_run(...)` unconditionally. CI is therefore executed twice on the same tree. If the first run passes and the second `ci_run` flakes or otherwise fails, `_run_checks` parks an entry whose required CI gate already passed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_run.py:129 (`_run_checks`)

chunk_findings.detail: After `land` has already merged the entry, the new `finish_item` call can raise an exception (for example, an `OSError` while writing the completion record). That exception is caught by `_one`’s broad `except Exception`, which sets `state = MQ.PARKED` even though the merge already succeeded. The entry is recorded as parked, so a resumed item can be merged again later; this contradicts the new code’s own intent that a post-merge completion failure must remain `MQ.MERGED`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_run.py:203 (`_one`)

chunk_findings.detail:
A release request is silently not applied when the item is already `RUNNING`. The `waiting` search matches both `QUEUED` and `RUNNING`, but the release branch only marks the entry when `waiting.state == QUEUED`:

```python
if release is not None and not waiting.released and waiting.state == QUEUED:
    ...
return waiting, False
```

Input that demonstrates it: an entry for item `I` is already in `RUNNING` state. Calling `add(repo, "I", ..., release={"author": "bot", "lane": "LC-wake", "tree": "abc"})` returns `(waiting, False)` with `waiting.released == False` and no error. A caller cannot distinguish this from a successful release without an extra check, so the choosing agent may leave its lease after `add` returns; the entry has no `released`/`lane`/`tree`, so on a later machine-gate failure there is no lane wake target. This contradicts the function’s contract that `release` marks the entry released.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergequeue.py:add

chunk_findings.detail: `release=bool(a.get("release"))` collapses "not provided" to `False`, so the CLI can never invoke the new release-by-policy path from `lanes.release_mode`. With `lanes.release_mode` configured to release items without the flag, running `ddflow queue add <item>` (no `--release`) calls `api.queue_add(..., release=False)`; the raw `None` that means "consult policy" is lost, so the item is not released and the lane stays blocked. Pass `a.get("release")` unchanged so the absent flag remains `None`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/mergequeue.py:28

chunk_findings.detail: The declared default `new = '["standards"]'` omits `ci` and `unit_tests`, even though the change's own intent says the integrator runs the remaining machine gates `(ci, unit_tests, standards)`. An item whose judgement gates are recorded and still has `ci`/`unit_tests` remaining will not have all its remaining machine gates recognized by this knob; the default should include all three, otherwise valid release-at-enqueue cases are refused or the queue does not owe those gates.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lanes.release_machine_gates.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The test never asserts that `recover` returned exit code `0` or that the entry actually left `MQ.RUNNING`. Given a recover command that fails nonzero and prints `T1` in an error message, `assert "T1" in out + err` and `assert MQ.get(rp, "T1").released is True` still pass because the `released` flag was already true before the failed recover. The test therefore does not catch a broken recovery path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_release_at_enqueue.py::test_a_crashed_integrator_leaves_the_released_item_for_recover

chunk_findings.detail: `freed = _hand_over(...) if plan and entry.released else {}` ignores `added`. A second `ddflow queue add --release ITEM` for an item that is already queued and already released will produce `added=False` and `entry.released=True`; `_hand_over` then runs again, appending a duplicate `lane.released_for_gate` event, calling `L.release` again, and sending a duplicate `LR.notify`. Existing queue.add is idempotent for re-adds ("was already queued"), so release side effects should happen only when this call newly enqueues or newly releases the item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_add.py:124

chunk_findings.detail: `_hand_over` is called after `MQ.add` has already persisted the queue entry and marked it released, but none of `_hand_over`'s I/O (`log.append`, `L.release`, `LR.notify`) is guarded. If `LR.notify` fails to write to the lane inbox, or `L.release` returns false/raises because the lease is still held, `queue_add` raises after the item is queued and `entry.released=True`. The caller sees a failed command even though custody was already handed to the merge queue; if the lease release actually failed, the agent still holds the lease while the queue operates on the item, recreating the hold-and-wait state this change is meant to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_add.py:124

chunk_findings.detail: For a released entry with `ci` in `effective_pipeline` and `it.gate_outcome("ci") != "passed"`, the new loop calls `run_gate(repo, it.id, "ci", agent=agent)`. If that run passes, control falls through to the pre-existing `if "ci" in pipe:` block, which unconditionally calls `ci_run(...)` on the same `it.id`. The same CI check therefore runs twice on the same commit. A CI server that rejects duplicate builds, or a transient failure in the second run, parks the item even though the newly added gate run already passed. The released path should skip the existing `ci_run` when the new `run_gate` already ran that gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_run.py _run_checks

chunk_findings.detail: `_judgement` builds `asked` as `[g for g in cfg.lanes.release_gates if g in s.pipeline and g not in s.not_applicable]` and then only checks the gates that survive the filter. A required judgement gate that `G.status` puts in `s.not_applicable` (or does not put in `s.pipeline`) is silently ignored, so `_judgement` can return `""` and release proceeds with no recorded `passed`/`skipped` outcome for that gate. For example, if `critic` is not applicable in this repo and is listed in `s.not_applicable`, an item with no critic record is released even though the module contract says release is refused unless each judgement gate is recorded passed on the current tree or skipped with its reason.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:_judgement

chunk_findings.detail: `after_run` calls `notify(...)` and then discards the returned `why`. When the lane inbox is at `cfg.lease.inbox_max_pending`, `IB.send` returns a non-empty full-inbox reason and does not enqueue the resume brief; the released item remains `MQ.PARKED`, but the lane receives no wake and no `resume_brief`. This is exactly the failure the `notify` doc says must not happen ("a full inbox must not undo a release or hide a parked item"), and it can leave a parked item unclaimed indefinitely.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:after_run

chunk_findings.detail: `_claim_slot(every, item, release_cap)` runs before `waiting` is inspected and before the only existing-entry path that actually marks an entry released (`waiting.state == QUEUED and not waiting.released`). As a result it can raise `SlotsFull` for an operation that would consume no slot. Concrete input: `release_cap=1`; item B is already released and QUEUED (holding the sole slot); item A is already RUNNING but not released. Calling `add(repo, "A", agent=..., release={...}, release_cap=1)` reaches `_claim_slot`, computes `held=1` from B, and raises `SlotsFull`. But the subsequent code would not mark A because `A.state == RUNNING`; the released-slot count stays 1, so the call should instead return the existing RUNNING entry unchanged. The capacity check is applied to a no-op release.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergequeue.py:add

chunk_findings.detail: The default `lanes.release_machine_gates` is `["standards"]`, but the change’s own intent says the machine gates the integrator finishes are `ci`, `unit_tests`, and `standards` (while `lanes.release_gates` covers only the judgement gates). With this default, an item whose only remaining gates are `ci` and `unit_tests`—the normal case for release-at-enqueue—would not be classified as having only machine gates remaining, so the release would be refused and the lane would not be freed. The default is incomplete and should include `ci` and `unit_tests`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lanes.release_machine_gates.toml:5

chunk_findings.detail: The test calls `run_cli(rp, "recover")` but never asserts its return code; it only checks that `"T1" in out + err` and that the saved entry still has `released is True`. A regressed `recover` command that exits non-zero and prints an error mentioning `T1` causes this test to pass even though recovery failed, because the released item still exists and still has `released is True`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_release_at_enqueue.py:test_a_crashed_integrator_leaves_the_released_item_for_recover

chunk_findings.detail: `_hand_over` and the modified `queue_add` text use `LR` (`LR.ready_text`, `LR.EVENT`, `LR.event_data`, `LR.machine_gates`, `LR.notify`), but this diff does not add an import for `LR`. `ddflow/services/lanerelease.py` is itself a new file in this change, so `LR` cannot have been a pre-existing import. On any eligible release-at-enqueue path, `_hand_over` reaches `log.append(LR.EVENT, ...)` and raises `NameError: name 'LR' is not defined`, aborting the command before the lease release is recorded and leaving the item enqueued while the agent lease is still held.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_add.py:_hand_over

chunk_findings.detail:
The release safety check silently drops any `cfg.lanes.release_gates` entry that is absent from `s.pipeline`:

```python
asked = [g for g in cfg.lanes.release_gates if g in s.pipeline and g not in s.not_applicable]
```

That makes the check fail open. For example, with `[lanes].release_gates = ["rubber_duck", "critic"]` where `critic` is not present in `s.pipeline` (a typo, a gate removed from the pipeline, or a temporarily disabled gate), `critic` is never examined. An item with only `rubber_duck` passed gets `""` from `_judgement` and is released, even though a configured mandatory judgement gate was never recorded. The module's own contract says release is refused unless each configured judgement gate is recorded passed/skipped; this path does not refuse.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:55 (`_judgement`)

chunk_findings.detail: For a released entry, the new loop runs every `LR.machine_gates(cfg)` gate that is also in `effective_pipeline` via `run_gate`. Since the release machine gates are stated/intended to include `ci` and `unit_tests`, and the code immediately afterward still runs the pre-existing hard-coded `if "ci" in pipe` and unit-tests paths, that same CI/unit_tests check can be executed twice on the same integrated ref. Concretely, a released item with `ci` owed will get `run_gate("ci")` followed by `ci_run`; the second submission can fail because a duplicate build is already running, parking a clean merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_run.py:132-136

chunk_findings.detail: The new `[lanes]` knobs `release_max`, `release_gates`, and `release_machine_gates` are declared without `strictest`, but the change's intent requires “company floors tighten-only” for knobs under `[lanes]`. `release_mode` defines a tightening floor (`strictest=("off", ...)`), while these three do not, so in a merged configuration a subordinate or agent config can widen `release_max` (for example, a company floor of `release_max = 1` overridden by an agent config of `10`) or remove required gates from `release_gates`/`release_machine_gates`, defeating the company’s restrictive floor.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/lanes.py: release_max, release_gates, release_machine_gates

chunk_findings.detail: The `asked` list comprehension at `asked = [g for g in cfg.lanes.release_gates if g in s.pipeline and g not in s.not_applicable]` silently drops any configured `[lanes].release_gates` entry that is absent from `G.status(...).pipeline`. If a required judgement gate is missing from the loaded pipeline—for example `[lanes] release_gates = ["rubber_duck", "critic"]` while the loaded pipeline only contains `rubber_duck` because `critic` was removed or mistyped—`_judgement` never checks `critic` and returns `""`, so the item is released without that required judgement gate. The safety check should fail closed for an unknown configured gate, not ignore it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:_judgement

chunk_findings.detail: When `add(..., release=...)` sees an already-waiting QUEUED entry, it mutates the in-memory `waiting` object read under `_entries_locked` and calls `_write(repo, waiting)`. `_entries_locked` is the `add.lock`, but the queue run path can transition that same entry to RUNNING under its own lock outside `add.lock`. Interleaving: run writes `state=RUNNING` for item A after `add` has called `entries(repo)` but before `add` calls `_write(repo, waiting)`. `add` then writes back the stale `QUEUED` state with `released=True`, undoing the RUNNING transition while an integrator is already working the item. The item can then be picked again by another integrator, causing duplicate execution or a duplicate merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergequeue.py:add (release branch)

chunk_findings.detail: `release=bool(a.get("release"))` collapses the tri-state release parameter into a two-state bool. When the `--release` flag is omitted, `a.get("release")` is `None`, so the API receives `False`, indistinguishable from an explicit `--release=false`. This means by-policy release cannot ever happen through this declared surface: `ddflow queue add <id>` with `lanes.release_mode` configured to release does not release the agent, contradicting the intent's "ddflow queue add --release (or by policy)".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/mergequeue.py:28

chunk_findings.detail: `mine = {"ci", "merge", *also} | ({"unit_tests"} if unit_tests else set())` adds every gate in `also` to the integrator-produced set regardless of the `unit_tests` flag. If `also` contains `"unit_tests"` (as `lanes.release_machine_gates` does per the intent) and `unit_tests` is `False` (`--no-unit-tests`), `owed_gates` omits the unsettled `unit_tests` gate. Thus `ddflow queue add --release --no-unit-tests <id>` can enqueue/release an item with `unit_tests` never settled, and the integrator also will not run it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergequeue.py owed_gates

chunk_findings.detail: The default `lanes.release_machine_gates` is set to `["standards"]`, but the change intent defines the remaining machine gates as `ci, unit_tests, standards`. With this default, a lane that has not overridden the knob will only treat `standards` as a machine gate after release; an item with `ci` and `unit_tests` still pending can be released and merged without those gates being run. The default list should include `ci` and `unit_tests` as well.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lanes.release_machine_gates.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: In `test_a_crashed_integrator_leaves_the_released_item_for_recover`, the exit code from `run_cli(rp, "recover")` is assigned to `_code` but never asserted. A broken `recover` implementation could exit nonzero and not actually recover the item, yet the test would still pass: line 176 only checks that `"T1"` appears in stdout/stderr, and line 177 only re-reads `released=True` that the test itself saved on line 174 before invoking `recover`. The test therefore does not verify the recovery behavior it exists to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_release_at_enqueue.py:175

chunk_findings.detail: `_claim_slot(every, item, release_cap)` runs before `waiting` is inspected and before the only existing-entry path that actually marks an entry released (`waiting.state == QUEUED and not waiting.released`). chunk_findings.detail: `freed = _hand_over(...) if plan and entry.released else {}` ignores `added`. chunk_findings.detail: `_hand_over` is called after `MQ.add` has already persisted the queue entry and marked it released, but none of `_hand_over`'s I/O (`log.append`, `L.release`, `LR.notify`) is guarded. chunk_findings.detail: For a released entry with `ci` in `effective_pipeline` and `it.gate_outcome("ci") != "passed"`, the new loop calls `run_gate(repo, it.id, "ci", agent=agent)`. If that run passes, control falls through to the pre-existing `if "ci" in pipe:` block, which unconditionally calls `ci_run(...)` on the same `it.id`. The same CI check therefore runs twice on the same commit. A CI server that rejects duplicate builds, or a transient failure in the second run, parks the item even though the newly added gate run already passed. The released path should skip the existing `ci_run` when the new `run_gate` already ran that gate.

chunk_findings.detail: `_judgement` builds `asked` as `[g for g in cfg.lanes.release_gates if g in s.pipeline and g not in s.not_applicable]` and then only checks the gates that survive the filter.
